newsitem.title: CUBA: Cuba recognizes Kabila's new government.
newsitem.headline: Cuba recognizes Kabila's new government.

text.p: Cuba, which supported Laurent Kabila's failed rebel struggle in Zaire in the 1960s, on Wednesday recognised Kabila's government and the new Democratic Republic of Congo.

A Foreign Ministry statement said Havana recognised the new government of the Democratic Republic of Congo, while "expressing the desire that it is able to install the necessary peace and stability to lead the people towards a prosperous and just society."
The statement was published in the ruling Communist Party daily Granma.
Kabila, whose rebel forces toppled dictator Mobutu Sese Seko at the weekend after a seven-month war, changed the name of the country from Zaire and declared himself its leader.
Cuba's links with Kabila, 56, go back to the late Argentine-born revolutionary Ernesto "Che" Guevara.
Guevara, hero of Cuba's 1959 revolution, fought alongside Kabila in a rebel struggle in eastern Zaire in the early 1960s.
Guevara was initially impressed by Kabila but swiftly became disillusioned by him and his then ragged rebel band before they and the Cubans were defeated by foreign mercenaries in 1965.
Guevara was killed in another abortive rebel uprising in Bolivia in 1967.
